A_H8.reasoning: Schedule H8 drops the simplex link grantor->c2 in Step 3 (leaving c2->grantor and all other links up), has c2 request in Step 4, and arms Step 5 ({at: {event: Grant, client: c2}, do: {cell: F1.1, crash: grantor}}) expecting the grantor to process c2's request, emit Grant(c2, t2), and lose the reply on the down grantor->c2 link, which would then crash the grantor so the two remaining lease nodes elect a new leader connected to c2. Instead, neither side emits Grant(c2) when grantor->c2 is down: the model guards Grant(n, c) on bidirectional Conn(n, c) (documented in model/README.md X2.4 as an under-approximation to avoid unbounded grant retries), while the implementation allocates a token on the grantor but suppresses emitting a Grant event when the reply send over grantor->c2 fails (documented in impl/README.md Interpretation 71). Because Grant(c2) is never emitted, Step 5 never fires and the grantor never crashes. In the resulting state after Step 3 (the last fault actually executed), the two follower lease nodes ({n1, n3} in the model; {n2, n3} in the implementation), storage s, and requester c2 are all up and pairwise bidirectionally connected, so C1.4's premise holds literally under failure-model-v2.md and schedule-format.md Rule L3 (which explicitly states that the connected majority need not include the current grantor and the requester need not be connected to it). However, because the un-crashed grantor remains bidirectionally connected to both followers, its CheckQuorum check stays satisfied and both followers continue to hear it (suppressing elections via HearsLeader and voter stickiness), while neither side relays grants through followers or steps down when a leader cannot reach a requester (the exact failure mode predicted in model/README.md X2.5). Thus c2 never receives a grant, genuinely violating C1.4 on both sides.

A_H8.stall_mechanism: After the simplex fault drop: [[grantor, c2]], neither side emits a Grant(c2) event while grantor->c2 is down (the model guards Grant(n, c) on bidirectional Conn(n, c) per X2.4; the implementation suppresses emitting Grant when the reply send on grantor->c2 fails per Interpretation 71), so Step 5 (crash: grantor on Grant(c2)) never triggers. The un-crashed grantor remains bidirectionally connected to both follower lease nodes—satisfying CheckQuorum and preventing follower elections—while unable to deliver a grant to c2 over the down link grantor->c2 or relay it through the followers.
A_H8.what_would_settle_it: To overturn this explained verdict, one would have to show either (1) that C1.4's premise under failure-model-v2.md and Rule L3 does not hold when two lease nodes, storage, and c2 form a bidirectional clique that excludes the current grantor (contradicting Rule L3's explicit text), or (2) that the inputs/interface forbid emitting Grant when the reply link is down AND treat an unreached fault step (Step 5) as invalidating C1.4's premise even though connectivity is already stable after Step 3.
